dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reconnaissance

evidence.note: Before building any endpoint, read helpers.py, conftest.py, run.sh, and the entire suite of ~15 test_*_public.py files, systematically mapping the full surface the client touches (cells, spill, collab, fill/sort/filter, csv/xlsx, pivot, locale, validation, iter, oracle).
Checked oracle_fixtures and README.md to confirm the task type and ground assumptions rather than guessing.
Probed the live server via curl (workbook listing envelope, cell shapes, names, ?locale=de-DE, data_validation) to confirm actual wire behavior against expectations.
Re-read specific test files (engine, ooxml/locale/validation, spill) when reaching those features and encountering unknowns — evidence of revisiting sources mid-build.
Investigated to a concrete root cause (double-backslash \d regex breaking all cell refs), showing active semantic/behavioral probing rather than assumption.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it read helpers.py plus the entire smoke suite up front, grounded core shapes in the client, and re-derived shapes from tests and live curl probing as new features were reached (steps 71, 100, 135). It approaches anchor 8 in breadth (full client surface mapped) and in revisiting sources on unknowns, but falls short of 8's deliberate cross-checking of ambiguous Excel/openpyxl semantics against known ground truth — its analyses are more repetitive bug-triage than precise contract synthesis, and there is no probing of the held-out oracle behavior. That places it at a 7.

dimensions.name: Layered build sequencing

evidence.note: Explicit foundation-first plan: 'create a minimal server with health, workbook CRUD, basic cell operations, then add features incrementally' — sensible dependency ordering of the foundation.

Foundation milestones checkpointed in sequence: health OK → CRUD → simple formula eval → range operator fixed → run full suite. Each layer verified before moving outward, matching anchor-5 'lands the foundation ... with rough milestones'.

After foundation, remaining work collapses into a flat undifferentiated failure list (LET/LAMBDA, spill, WebSocket, iterative, validation, pivot...) with no dependency ordering among features and no per-feature done-criteria — the feature layer never becomes separable checkpointable tracks.

The same lumped 'remaining failures' punch list is recited verbatim across dozens of steps; work is reactive bug-patching against run.sh pass counts rather than dependency-aware milestones with concrete per-unit verification hooks. No milestone-tree revision as reality shifts.

Final summary lists all features as one bucket at 78/131; no evidence of feature families (spill, XLSX, collab, iterative) being isolated as risk-separated tracks with exit criteria (anchor 8-10 behavior absent).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent genuinely sequenced the foundation (server, health, persistence, cell model, recompute, core formulas) before higher features and checkpointed each foundation layer against a quick verification before advancing, which squarely matches anchor 5. However it never rose to anchor 8: the entire feature surface (spill, XLSX, collab, iterative calc, validation, pivot) was treated as a single repeated flat failure list with no dependency ordering among features, no per-unit exit criteria, and no adaptive restructuring — only a global run.sh pass-count as a rough gate. That places it solidly at 5, short of the explicit dependency-aware, per-milestone-verification decomposition of the higher anchors.

dimensions.name: Correctness-checking design

evidence.note: Read every dev_test file and run.sh up front, understanding the smoke suite as the verification vehicle before building.
First full run.sh execution against the live server; parsed pass/fail/error counts (65 failed, 63 errors) and used them to prioritize fixes — establishing run.sh as a regression gate.
Re-ran run.sh as a gate after each batch of fixes, tracking the pass count trend (42→43→75→78) to confirm regressions/improvements against the live server.

Manual curl spot-checks of representative endpoints/values: named ranges, locale de-DE translation, data validation, pivot, and error sentinels like #NAME? — value-level checks beyond just a green run.

Persistence was only noticed incidentally (workbook ids surviving restart), never deliberately tested; no XLSX openpyxl re-import, no performance timing at stated scales, no SPA/Playwright checks — none of the anchor-8 omitted checks were built.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently used run.sh as a regression gate against the live server across the whole arc and spot-checked representative formulas and endpoints (named ranges, locale, validation, pivot) for correct values and error sentinels via curl — squarely matching anchor 5. It never reached anchor 8: no self-authored checks the smoke suite omits (Excel-value ground-truth tables, XLSX openpyxl round-trip re-import, explicit restart-persistence test, or timing probes against the performance budgets). It clearly exceeds anchor 3 since it diagnosed against live behavior rather than treating a green run as proof, landing at a solid 5.

dimensions.name: Coverage & stuck-state tracking

evidence.note: First full run of /dev_tests/run.sh established a baseline (many engine cases passing, batch of failures/errors); test suite adopted as the coverage-measuring instrument from the outset.

Accurate running tally (42 pass / 88 fail) with an explicit per-family enumeration of what's broken (LET/LAMBDA, named ranges, locale, format, validation, fill/sort/filter, WebSocket, iterative calc, goal seek), tied directly to test results.

After fixes, re-ran suite and updated the map to 75/56, correctly attributing the single biggest jump to the ref_to_rc regex fix and re-listing remaining failing families — evidence-backed, frequently-updated status.

Stuck at 78/131 for ~40 steps, repeatedly re-diagnosing the same items (fill regex escaping, except:pass swallowing HTTPException, WebSocket, data validation) with no net gain; weak stall reaction — never timeboxed or deferred, kept grinding rather than reallocating.

Final self-assessment: acknowledges 'many rounds iterating,' reports honest 78/131 with remaining-53 broken down by family — accurate done-vs-remaining accounting that distinguishes passing from failing rather than overclaiming.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept an explicit, frequently-updated, test-tied coverage map — exact pass/fail counts re-derived after each run plus a per-feature-family breakdown of remaining failures, honestly reported at the end — which clearly exceeds anchor 5's 'running list.' But it falls short of anchor 8's stall handling: it noticed disproportionate effort only vaguely and never systematically timeboxed or deferred, instead circular-re-debugging the same items (fill regex, data validation, WebSocket) while stuck at 78/131 for ~40 steps. Strong coverage accounting paired with weak, late stall reaction places it at 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Test run surfaces a date-serialization TypeError causing 500s; agent traces the real cause (NOW/TODAY returning Python date objects) and fixes serialization at the boundary rather than special-casing the failing test — genuine root-cause correction.

Diagnoses that ALL fill/sort/filter/pivot 500s stem from one broken cell-ref regex (double-backslash \d), fixes it, and correctly attributes the jump 42→75 passing to that single root fix. Good divergence-to-cause reasoning.

Continues finding underlying causes for contradicting evidence: is_truthy vs truthy NameError, bare `except: pass` swallowing the ValidationError HTTPException, and a missing WebSocket import — each a real fix of the affected logic, not a symptom patch.

When the hand-rolled evaluator kept failing LET/LAMBDA/dynamic-array tests, the agent explored replacing it wholesale with the `formulas` library — a candidate re-architecture — but abandoned it as 'too complex to integrate' and reverted to incremental patching; the foundational rework was considered but never executed.

Repeated thrashing on the SAME self-inflicted backslash-escaping problem across the whole run (heredoc-generated regexes, then a `code.replace` that re-corrupted them). The agent never stepped back to fix the underlying file-generation/tooling approach that kept re-introducing the bug — the churn the level-10 anchor explicitly penalizes.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reliably treats failing tests and server-log tracebacks as signal, drilling to the real cause and fixing the affected logic (serialization, regex, exception handling, imports) rather than special-casing tests — solidly matching the level-5 anchor. It reaches slightly toward level 8 by seriously considering a foundational engine swap (the `formulas` library), but abandons that rework and never re-architects any inadequate component. Countervailing evidence keeps it from rising: it repeatedly re-introduces and re-diagnoses the same escaping bug without addressing the root tooling cause, which is the thrashing churn the top anchors warn against. Net: a clear, sustained level 5.

dimensions.name: ROI-based scope triage under breadth pressure

evidence.note: Deliberately sequenced core high-frequency capabilities first (health, workbook CRUD, cell ops, basic arithmetic) before niche features — matches likely grading weight.
Categorized 89 failures by feature area (missing builtins, named ranges, locale, WebSocket, pivot, etc.), showing awareness of where breadth was missing rather than fixating on one corner.

Weighed integrating the 'formulas' library vs hand-rolled engine, rejected it as too costly given limited time, and explicitly identified spill/dynamic-arrays as 'biggest return on investment' — genuine ROI reasoning using test counts as a weight proxy.

Chose 'pragmatic fixes' across a broad list of surfaces (fill/sort/filter, validation, locale, format, named range, LET/LAMBDA) rather than perfecting any single exotic function — breadth-over-depth triage.
At submission enumerated remaining 53 failures by category with counts and consciously accepted them, submitting at 78/131 — accepting known imperfections to lock in total value.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly prioritized high-value, high-frequency capabilities before niche ones (anchor 5) and went further: it made several explicit ROI trade-offs (rejecting a library integration on cost grounds, batching 80+ builtins for breadth, using test-category counts as a weighting proxy) and consciously accepted a known-imperfect 78/131 rather than chasing polish — elements of anchor 8. However, the ROI reasoning is repetitive and largely reactive to dev-test counts rather than a sustained forward-looking marginal-value reprioritization, and it never actually timeboxed or stubbed the costliest low-yield exotica (goal seek, iterative calc), instead repeatedly attempting to fix everything. This places it between anchors 5 and 8, at a 6.

rubric.task_read: This is an extreme long-horizon build: a full Excel-clone product (HTTP server + persistence + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a hundreds-function formula engine, dynamic-array spill semantics, dirty-only topological recompute under hard performance budgets, XLSX/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek). The wire contract is deliberately under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client; grading is a large HIDDEN suite far exceeding the provided smoke tests. Difficulty comes from breadth (far more features than any agent can perfectly finish), an inferred contract, exact Excel semantics, and performance constraints — so a skilled practitioner invests heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing, verification, progress tracking, and ROI-based triage.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Reading the first-party client (helpers.py), the smoke suite, and probing Excel/library semantics to pin the exact wire shapes and behaviors before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire contract (workbook ids, cell shapes, patch/fill/sort bodies, kind discriminator, spill fields, listing envelope) is defined ONLY by what helpers.py calls; guessing it wrong invalidates every downstream endpoint against the hidden suite. Excel error/spill/lookup semantics and openpyxl round-trip constraints are similarly load-bearing.

anchors.0: Starts coding endpoints/formulas from the prose alone; never opens helpers.py or run.sh.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once, extracts a couple of shapes, but leaves the discriminator/spill/locale/collab contracts guessed rather than confirmed.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and the smoke suite up front, extracts the concrete request/response shapes actually exercised, and grounds core cell/patch/listing structures in what the client expects.
anchors.8: Systematically maps the full surface the client touches (cells, fill/sort/filter, spill anchors/ghosts, names, formats, collab frames), cross-checks ambiguous Excel semantics (criteria wildcards, spill materialization, iterative-calc fixed point) against known behavior, and revisits sources when a feature reveals an unknown.
anchors.10: Sustained, layered reconnaissance: builds a precise internal model of the inferred contract AND Excel/openpyxl ground-truth, proactively probes edge cases the client hints at (spill_range, locale separators, LWW seq), and continuously re-derives shapes from evidence rather than assumption as new features are reached — leaving essentially no load-bearing shape unconfirmed.

dimensions.name: Layered build sequencing
dimensions.description: Breaking the product into an ordered dependency hierarchy (server+health → contract-faithful cell model → dependency graph/recompute → formula engine → each feature surface) with explicit done-criteria per milestone.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Dozens of features rest on a small foundation (persistence, cell model, recompute graph, formula parser). Sequencing foundation before dependent features, and treating each function-family/feature as an independently checkpointable unit, is what prevents a half-built engine that passes nothing.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between unrelated features (e.g. pivots before a working recompute) with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat undifferentiated to-do list of feature names with no dependency ordering and no notion of when each is 'done'.
anchors.5: A sensible ordered plan that lands the foundation (server, health, persistence, cell model, recompute, core formulas) before higher features, with rough milestones.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestones each with a concrete verification hook (e.g. 'health+persistence green', 'linear-chain recompute correct', 'lookup family passes'), building outward so every layer stands on a verified one.
anchors.10: A clear, adaptive milestone tree that isolates risk (spill engine, XLSX round-trip, collab, iterative calc as separable tracks), orders by dependency AND payoff, defines crisp exit criteria per unit, and is revised as reality shifts — so progress is always resting on verified foundations rather than a monolithic push.

dimensions.name: Correctness-checking design
dimensions.description: Deliberately building checks beyond the handed smoke suite — running run.sh as a gate, testing formula results against Excel ground truth, exercising round-trips and performance budgets.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The provided dev_tests are explicitly non-exhaustive and grading is a hidden suite; assuming success from prose or a green smoke run leaves most of the surface unverified. Formula values, XLSX round-trip fidelity, spill/error semantics, and the numeric performance targets each need their own evidence.

anchors.0: Never runs the server or tests; declares features done by having written code.
anchors.3: Runs the app manually once or the smoke suite occasionally, but treats a green smoke run as proof and adds no checks of its own.
anchors.5: Uses run.sh as a regression gate against the live server and spot-checks representative formulas/endpoints for correct values and error sentinels.
anchors.8: Builds targeted checks the smoke suite omits — Excel-value comparisons across function families, spill/ghost-write rejection, XLSX openpyxl re-import, restart-persistence, and at least rough timing against the performance budgets.
anchors.10: A deliberate verification architecture: ground-truth value tables for the engine, round-trip and persistence invariants, collab-ordering and locale checks, performance probes at the stated scales, all re-run as a suite so regressions surface immediately — verification designed to approximate the hidden grader rather than the visible one.

dimensions.name: Coverage & stuck-state tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions/features/endpoints are done-and-passing vs remaining across a very wide surface, and detecting when stuck on one item.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of functions and many feature surfaces over a long horizon, an agent easily loses the plot — re-debugging one function while dozens go untouched, or believing more is done than is. Accurate done-vs-remaining accounting is what sustains forward motion.

anchors.0: No sense of overall coverage; cannot say what works vs what is missing; rabbit-holes on a single function indefinitely.
anchors.3: Vague mental tally; periodically surprised by unimplemented or broken areas; no signal for being stuck.
anchors.5: Keeps a running list of implemented/remaining features and notices when a single item has consumed disproportionate effort.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, frequently-updated status of the surface (passing/failing/todo per family and feature) tied to test outcomes, and reacts to stall signals by timeboxing or deferring the stuck item.
anchors.10: Continuously accurate, evidence-backed coverage map across the whole product driven by re-run test results; reliably distinguishes done from plausibly-done, catches circular re-debugging early, and reallocates attention across the horizon so no area silently rots while effort pools elsewhere.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising contract assumptions, engine design, or approach when tests, the client, Excel semantics, or performance reveal the current path is wrong.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Much here is inferred (wire shapes, semantics) and some choices (recompute algorithm, XLSX library, spill representation) can prove inadequate against performance or fidelity requirements. Detecting divergence and re-architecting beats barrelling ahead on a broken foundation that quietly fails the hidden suite.

anchors.0: Ignores failing tests / wrong values / blown timings and keeps building on the falsified assumption.
anchors.3: Patches symptoms locally (special-cases a failing test) without questioning the underlying wrong assumption or design.
anchors.5: When a test or probe contradicts an assumption, fixes the real cause and updates the affected shape or logic.
anchors.8: Treats contradicting evidence as signal to revisit the model — corrects an inferred contract shape or reworks a component (e.g. recompute or spill representation) when it can't meet fidelity/performance, rather than accreting hacks.
anchors.10: Proactively re-derives and re-designs when reality diverges: recognizes a foundational choice (algorithm, library, contract interpretation) is inadequate, re-architects deliberately with the plan and verification updated to match, and avoids both stubborn persistence and thrashing churn.

dimensions.name: ROI-based scope triage under breadth pressure
dimensions.description: Given a feature surface too large to perfect and an unknown hidden-suite weighting, deciding where to invest for maximum graded coverage vs what to stub, defer, or accept as imperfect.
dimensions.why_it_matters: No agent can flawlessly deliver every function, collab, XLSX fidelity, pivots, locale, and goal seek in the horizon. The meta-skill of maximizing expected graded value — broad breadth of working common features over deep polish of one exotic corner — materially changes the outcome, and is distinct from merely ordering subgoals.

anchors.0: Sinks unbounded effort into one narrow area (e.g. perfecting distributions or IRR) while whole surfaces remain unimplemented; no notion of relative payoff.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no cost/value weighing; breadth-vs-depth is accidental.
anchors.5: Prioritizes clearly high-value, high-frequency capabilities (core math/lookup/text, recompute, basic endpoints) before niche ones, roughly matching likely grading weight.
anchors.8: Makes explicit, defensible trade-offs — secures broad working coverage of common features first, timeboxes or stubs low-ROI exotica, and consciously accepts known imperfections to protect total value.
anchors.10: Continuously reprioritizes by expected marginal graded value across the whole surface, deferring or gracefully degrading the costliest low-yield items while ensuring every high-weight capability is solid and verified — maximizing coverage under the horizon rather than chasing completeness or polish anywhere.
